title: Papunya Tula art movement
summary: In 1971 at Papunya, west of Alice Springs, schoolteacher Geoffrey Bardon encouraged men to paint a blank school wall. Senior Aboriginal men painted a Honey Ant Dreaming mural, and many more began painting. In 1972 the artists formed their own company, owned by people of the Luritja and Pintupi language groups. Sacred symbols are removed from works shown publicly.
